q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-17. Q2 FY2027 ends on July 26, 2026 (already passed), so the earnings release with forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 has likely already occurred or is imminent. The question asks about the forward guidance announced in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release, which would have been announced around late August 2026. Given that today is 2026-08-17, we are essentially at or just before the Q2 earnings announcement. **Resolution is immediate or within days.**

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The current research provides NVIDIA's actual Q2 FY2027 forward guidance announced on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%** (so $89.18B to $92.82B at the 2% bounds).

However, I need to carefully parse what the question is asking. It asks "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)" — this is asking for the forward guidance *announced* during the Q2 FY2027 earnings call, not the guidance *for* Q2 FY2027.

The research states guidance was given on May 20, 2026 for Q2 FY2027. The Q2 FY2027 earnings release (for the quarter ending July 26) would typically occur in late August 2026. At that Q2 earnings call, NVIDIA would provide forward guidance for Q3 FY2027.

The research mentions:
- UBS is predicting Q3 FY2027 guidance could reach $107-108 billion
- This is based on steady Blackwell demand and fast Rubin platform ramp

The range provided (99.5 to 115.5 billion) brackets these expectations reasonably well, with the upper end potentially capturing upside scenarios.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Weaker-than-expected Data Center demand
- Geopolitical restrictions on China sales being more stringent than anticipated (they already assume zero China DC revenue)
- Competitive pressures from AMD or other vendors
- Supply chain constraints on Blackwell or Rubin
- Macro slowdown affecting AI spending
- Inventory corrections in the channel

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Faster-than-expected Rubin ramp (as UBS suggests)
- Stronger enterprise adoption of AI accelerators
- Potential relaxation of China export restrictions
- Higher pricing power if demand outpaces supply
- Unexpected wins in new markets (automotive, robotics, etc.)
- Better-than-expected Blackwell sustainability through Q3

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q2 FY2027 guidance given in May: $91.0B ± 2% ($89.18B - $92.82B)
- Average analyst estimate at that time: $86.84B
- UBS bull case for Q3 FY2027: $107-108B
- The range given (99.5B - 115.5B) suggests the questioner expects sequential guidance growth

NVIDIA typically grows Q-over-Q in this part of the fiscal year. The May guidance of ~$91B for Q2 (July quarter) to potential $107-108B for Q3 (October quarter) represents ~18-20% sequential growth, which would be consistent with strong Blackwell momentum.

## Analysis

The most likely scenario is that in the Q2 FY2027 earnings call (late August 2026), NVIDIA will provide forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 in the range of $105-110 billion, reflecting:
- Continued strong Blackwell demand
- Early Rubin contribution
- Normal seasonal patterns for the October quarter
- The UBS estimate of $107-108B is well-reasoned and specifically cited for Q3 FY2027 guidance

The range floor (99.5B) seems low unless there's a significant deterioration in demand. The upper end (115.5B) would represent exceptionally strong execution, possible but less likely.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, as announced on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. This outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance is also reflected in the SEC filing for Q1 FY2027 [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).

This figure is above the average analyst estimate of $86.84 billion at the time of the Q1 earnings report [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). However, some analysts, such as UBS, are more bullish, predicting actual revenue for the quarter ending July 26 (Q2 FY2027) could be $94-95 billion, and October-quarter (Q3 FY2027) guidance could reach $107-108 billion. This optimism is based on steady Blackwell demand and an unexpectedly fast ramp-up of the next-gen Rubin platform [aliteq.com](https://aliteq.com/nvidia-q2-fy27-earnings-preview-ubs-2026).
